Almonty/ALM is a high-attention tungsten asset-owner benchmark, but later layers must distinguish concentrate and oxide exposure from actual APT processing control.
Kennametal/KMT is a mid-cap underfollowed downstream customer candidate: the key research question is whether tungsten scarcity is margin risk, pricing power, or a sourcing/recycling advantage.
American Resources/AREC belongs only in the speculative shadow lane until ReElement ownership economics, tungsten process product form, commercial scale, and customer commitments are verified.

Private processors Global Tungsten & Powders, Buffalo Tungsten, Wolfram Bergbau, Plansee, and possibly specialty gas suppliers may be more directly exposed than most US-listed equities; public-market mapping may require parent-company or customer proxies.

KMT is the best US-listed underfollowed downstream tungsten intermediate candidate found in this pass: explicit tungsten carbide powders, tungsten oxide reduction process, and recycling/production history.

ALM is a US-listed non-China upstream/oxide candidate, but current evidence supports concentrate and planned tungsten oxide rather than confirmed APT processing; treat as adjacent, not pure node exposure.
APD is a large-cap reference anchor for WF6 semiconductor demand pull, not an underfollowed APT processor.

The most direct non-China APT/recycling processor found, Global Tungsten & Powders, appears private within Plansee/Ceratizit; public-market exposure may be indirect through tooling, specialty gases, miners, or weak materials hypotheses.

Need a later evidence pass focused on actual APT capability, ore/feedstock source, customer qualification, and revenue materiality; many public candidates are downstream users or converters rather than APT processors.
KMT is the strongest US-listed underfollowed downstream candidate found in this pass: tungsten carbide powders and industrial/defense tooling exposure, but actual APT capability is unverified.
ALM is a useful allied tungsten feedstock candidate, but classify as upstream concentrate/oxide exposure until filings prove APT processing economics or direct downstream capture.
GMTL is a speculative-shadow US-listed tungsten development candidate because its public relevance is mainly through Nevada projects and a GTP offtake LOI, not current APT production.

APD is a large-cap reference anchor for tungsten hexafluoride, the semiconductor branch of the tungsten intermediate chain; use it to verify downstream tightness rather than as the main underfollowed candidate.

The key public-market gap is that the most direct APT processors identified, including Global Tungsten & Powders and Buffalo Tungsten/Wolfram, appear private or not cleanly US-listed; later layers should map their public suppliers, customers, lenders, and offtake partners.
KMT should be tracked as the cleanest US-listed underfollowed downstream tungsten powder/carbide converter for the APT bottleneck, pending validation of non-China feedstock and materiality.

ALM is a necessary reference anchor for non-China tungsten concentrate supply, but needs separation from the actual APT-processing bottleneck; confirm oxide/APT capability before upgrading node purity.
APD is a large-cap reference for WF6 semiconductor gas exposure; include mainly to map the APT-to-WF6 downstream path, not as an underfollowed small/mid-cap discovery candidate.
AREC/ReElement is a below-$300M speculative exception: include only as a shadow candidate until tungsten product form, throughput, customer qualification, and AREC economic ownership are verified.

Need a follow-up pass for private or foreign-listed processors such as Global Tungsten & Powders/Plansee and Buffalo Tungsten/Sandvik because the true APT/powder chokepoint may sit outside US-listed pure plays.

Layer 1B mapping suggests the investable US-listed public chain is fragmented: ALM for concentrate, KMT for carbide/powder conversion, APD for WF6 specialty gas, and AREC as speculative refining optionality.
